Subject: FinTrust RFI — vendor/cloud-provider ownership and evidence

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for taking the time to speak yesterday. As part of our final compliance review for the upcoming pilot, we need a short package that covers:

- Full vendor/subprocessor roster (current as of today) including service owner, region of processing, and whether they access customer data.
- Confirmation of primary cloud providers used in the hosted offering, and which subcomponents (storage, compute, telemetry) sit in each provider.
- Any planned changes in the next 90 days that could impact data residency or operator ownership.
- Evidence: a high-level dataflow diagram for the hosted API and any third-party storage endpoints.

Can you please send these materials (roster + diagram + brief narrative) by EOD Friday? If you prefer, we can route a short DocuSign/acceptance form after review.

We will share this with our InfoSec and Procurement teams. Let me know if you need more time.

Thanks,
Anna Lopez

FinTrust Financial Services

Mateo / Anna — attaching the roster and a draft dataflow per request. See notes below.

Attachments: vendor_roster_v2.xlsx (sheet: vendors, planned_changes), s3-dataflow-diagram.png

Key vendor highlights (short):
- Object storage: Primary: AWS S3 (us-west-2). Secondary replication to GCP (us-central1) for DR; S3 buckets are customer-isolated per-tenant prefix, server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) enabled.
- Compute/Serving: Hosted API runs on Dedicated GPU pools in both AWS and GCP depending on region routing policy. No model weights are persisted to third-party storage outside of our managed snapshot service (encrypted).
- Logging/Telemetry: Metrics and traces flow to an internal telemetry cluster (self-hosted) with exported aggregates to Datadog (no PII). Datadog access limited via role-scoped API keys.
- Third-party SaaS: Auth provider (Okta), Payment gateway (Stripe) — neither have access to model payloads. Several smaller vendors (monitoring, secrets rotation) have restricted API-level access for operational tasks.

Planned changes (next 90 days):
- Migrating a small percentage (~10% of new deployments) to a new GCP region (asia-southeast1) for APAC pilot (no customer data movement for existing tenants).
- Rolling out auto-rotating KMS keys for the snapshot service; no change to key ownership model (customer-managed KMS option remains for Private deployments).

I can expand any row in the roster with contracts and SOC/AOC references if FinTrust needs evidence.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure & Cloud Ops
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
